blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: PCSK1/PC1-3 deficiency with age-dependent enteric and endocrine phenotype

item.vignette: A 6-year-old boy had severe watery diarrhea and malabsorption beginning in the first weeks of life. The diarrhea gradually improved during infancy, but he subsequently developed intense hyperphagia and severe obesity. Laboratory testing now shows a markedly elevated fasting proinsulin-to-insulin ratio. His parents are healthy first cousins. Intestinal biopsy shows enteroendocrine cells but markedly reduced prohormone convertase 1/3 immunoreactivity.
item.lead_in: Which diagnosis best explains this age-dependent combination of gastrointestinal and endocrine findings?

options.B: Prohormone convertase 1/3 deficiency due to biallelic PCSK1 loss
options.E: Monogenic obesity due to MC4R loss of function

item.tested_construct: Biallelic PCSK1 loss causes prohormone convertase 1/3 deficiency, with severe congenital malabsorptive diarrhea early in life followed by hyperphagia, obesity, and multiple endocrine processing abnormalities including elevated proinsulin.

explanation.key_explanation: PCSK1 encodes prohormone convertase 1/3, a serine endoprotease required to process multiple prohormones and proneuropeptides. Severe biallelic loss can cause congenital malabsorptive diarrhea that improves with age, followed by hyperphagia and obesity; impaired proinsulin processing produces a high proinsulin-to-insulin ratio.

distractor_explanations.A: Option A proposes 'Congenital leptin deficiency'. It is not selected because it does not account for the distinctive transition from severe congenital malabsorptive diarrhea to hyperphagia/obesity together with elevated proinsulin and reduced PC1/3; Leptin deficiency causes severe early hyperphagia and obesity but does not explain neonatal malabsorptive diarrhea or impaired proinsulin processing.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. PCSK1 encodes prohormone convertase 1/3, a serine endoprotease required to process multiple prohormones and proneuropeptides. Severe biallelic loss can cause congenital malabsorptive diarrhea that improves with age, followed by hyperphagia and obesity; impaired proinsulin processing produces a high proinsulin-to-insulin ratio.
distractor_explanations.C: Option C proposes 'Proopiomelanocortin deficiency'. It is not selected because it does not account for the distinctive transition from severe congenital malabsorptive diarrhea to hyperphagia/obesity together with elevated proinsulin and reduced PC1/3; POMC deficiency causes adrenal insufficiency and hyperphagic obesity, often with pigmentary features, but not the characteristic congenital enteric phenotype and broad PC1/3 processing defect.
distractor_explanations.D: Option D proposes 'Congenital sucrase-isomaltase deficiency'. It is not selected because it does not account for the distinctive transition from severe congenital malabsorptive diarrhea to hyperphagia/obesity together with elevated proinsulin and reduced PC1/3; Sucrase-isomaltase deficiency causes carbohydrate-triggered osmotic diarrhea but does not evolve into a multisystem prohormone-processing endocrinopathy.
distractor_explanations.E: Option E proposes 'Monogenic obesity due to MC4R loss of function'. It is not selected because it does not account for the distinctive transition from severe congenital malabsorptive diarrhea to hyperphagia/obesity together with elevated proinsulin and reduced PC1/3; MC4R deficiency causes hyperphagic obesity but does not cause congenital malabsorptive diarrhea or a high proinsulin-to-insulin ratio from defective precursor processing.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize PCSK1 deficiency from congenital malabsorptive diarrhea that evolves toward hyperphagia/obesity with biochemical evidence of defective prohormone processing.

internal_content_path: Thyroid hormone metabolism and selenoprotein synthesis
blueprint.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: SECISBP2/SBP2 deficiency impairing selenocysteine incorporation and deiodinase activity

item.vignette: A 12-year-old boy is evaluated for short stature, delayed bone age, and mild developmental difficulties. Repeated thyroid studies show high-normal to elevated free thyroxine, low triiodothyronine, and a thyroid-stimulating hormone concentration within the reference range. Sequencing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in SECISBP2. Fibroblasts from the patient have reduced type 2 deiodinase activity.
item.lead_in: Which molecular process is most directly impaired by this mutation?

options.A: Iodination of thyroglobulin tyrosine residues by thyroid peroxidase
options.B: Transport of thyroid hormone into neurons by MCT8
options.C: Binding of triiodothyronine to thyroid hormone receptor beta
options.D: Insertion of selenocysteine into proteins including thyroid hormone deiodinases
options.E: Proteolytic release of thyroxine from iodinated thyroglobulin

item.tested_construct: SECISBP2 encodes SBP2, which is required for selenocysteine incorporation during selenoprotein synthesis; partial deficiency impairs selenoproteins such as deiodinases and disrupts peripheral thyroid hormone metabolism.

explanation.key_explanation: SBP2 participates in recoding UGA for selenocysteine incorporation into selenoproteins. Thyroid hormone deiodinases are selenoproteins, so SECISBP2 deficiency reduces deiodinase activity and can produce relatively high T4, low T3, and nonsuppressed TSH without a primary thyroid synthetic defect.

distractor_explanations.A: Option A proposes 'Iodination of thyroglobulin tyrosine residues by thyroid peroxidase'. It is not selected because it does not account for biallelic SECISBP2 loss with low T3, relatively high T4, normal TSH, and directly reduced deiodinase activity; Thyroid peroxidase defects cause dyshormonogenesis within the thyroid and do not explain a generalized selenoprotein synthesis defect with reduced deiodinase activity.
distractor_explanations.B: Option B proposes 'Transport of thyroid hormone into neurons by MCT8'. It is not selected because it does not account for biallelic SECISBP2 loss with low T3, relatively high T4, normal TSH, and directly reduced deiodinase activity; MCT8 is encoded by SLC16A2 and mediates cellular thyroid-hormone transport rather than selenocysteine incorporation.
distractor_explanations.C: Option C proposes 'Binding of triiodothyronine to thyroid hormone receptor beta'. It is not selected because it does not account for biallelic SECISBP2 loss with low T3, relatively high T4, normal TSH, and directly reduced deiodinase activity; THRB mutations alter nuclear thyroid-hormone signaling and feedback, not the biosynthesis of deiodinase selenoproteins.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. SBP2 participates in recoding UGA for selenocysteine incorporation into selenoproteins. Thyroid hormone deiodinases are selenoproteins, so SECISBP2 deficiency reduces deiodinase activity and can produce relatively high T4, low T3, and nonsuppressed TSH without a primary thyroid synthetic defect.
distractor_explanations.E: Option E proposes 'Proteolytic release of thyroxine from iodinated thyroglobulin'. It is not selected because it does not account for biallelic SECISBP2 loss with low T3, relatively high T4, normal TSH, and directly reduced deiodinase activity; Thyroglobulin proteolysis occurs in thyroid follicular cells and is not the process directly dependent on SECISBP2.

explanation.educational_objective: Link SECISBP2 deficiency to defective selenoprotein synthesis and reduced thyroid-hormone deiodinase activity.

blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: GNRHR loss causing pituitary GnRH resistance in normosmic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism

item.vignette: A 19-year-old man is evaluated for absent pubertal development. He has small testes, sparse facial hair, low serum testosterone, and low luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone. His sense of smell is normal, and MRI of the hypothalamic-pituitary region is normal. Genetic testing shows biallelic loss-of-function variants in GNRHR. Pulsatile administration of exogenous GnRH produces a markedly blunted gonadotropin response.
item.lead_in: Which physiologic defect most directly explains this patient's hypogonadism?

options.A: Reduced responsiveness of pituitary gonadotrophs to hypothalamic GnRH
options.B: Failed embryonic migration of GnRH neurons from the olfactory placode
options.C: Loss of kisspeptin-mediated depolarization of hypothalamic GnRH neurons
options.D: Failure of Leydig cells to respond to luteinizing hormone
options.E: Defective androgen receptor signaling in target tissues

item.tested_construct: Biallelic inactivating GNRHR variants cause normosmic isolated hypogonadotropic hypogonadism through pituitary gonadotroph resistance to GnRH rather than impaired GnRH-neuron migration.

explanation.key_explanation: GNRHR encodes the GnRH receptor on anterior pituitary gonadotrophs. Loss of receptor function prevents normal LH and FSH secretion in response to pulsatile hypothalamic GnRH, causing low sex steroids with low or inappropriately normal gonadotropins while olfaction remains intact.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. GNRHR encodes the GnRH receptor on anterior pituitary gonadotrophs. Loss of receptor function prevents normal LH and FSH secretion in response to pulsatile hypothalamic GnRH, causing low sex steroids with low or inappropriately normal gonadotropins while olfaction remains intact.
distractor_explanations.B: Option B proposes 'Failed embryonic migration of GnRH neurons from the olfactory placode'. It is not selected because it does not account for normal olfaction with biallelic GNRHR loss and a blunted gonadotropin response to exogenous pulsatile GnRH; Defective GnRH-neuron migration classically produces Kallmann syndrome with anosmia or hyposmia; this patient has normal olfaction and a receptor-level defect.
distractor_explanations.C: Option C proposes 'Loss of kisspeptin-mediated depolarization of hypothalamic GnRH neurons'. It is not selected because it does not account for normal olfaction with biallelic GNRHR loss and a blunted gonadotropin response to exogenous pulsatile GnRH; KISS1R dysfunction acts upstream at hypothalamic GnRH neurons; the identified mutation instead affects the pituitary receptor for GnRH itself.
distractor_explanations.D: Option D proposes 'Failure of Leydig cells to respond to luteinizing hormone'. It is not selected because it does not account for normal olfaction with biallelic GNRHR loss and a blunted gonadotropin response to exogenous pulsatile GnRH; LH-receptor failure causes primary gonadal dysfunction with elevated rather than low gonadotropins.
distractor_explanations.E: Option E proposes 'Defective androgen receptor signaling in target tissues'. It is not selected because it does not account for normal olfaction with biallelic GNRHR loss and a blunted gonadotropin response to exogenous pulsatile GnRH; Androgen receptor resistance causes impaired androgen action despite adequate or increased testosterone and gonadotropin drive, not a blunted pituitary response to GnRH.

explanation.educational_objective: Distinguish pituitary GnRH resistance from hypothalamic GnRH-neuron migration defects in normosmic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

evidence_map.claim: Correct. GNRHR encodes the GnRH receptor on anterior pituitary gonadotrophs. Loss of receptor function prevents normal LH and FSH secretion in response to pulsatile hypothalamic GnRH, causing low sex steroids with low or inappropriately normal gonadotropins while olfaction remains intact.

blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: Resistance to thyroid hormone alpha with tissue hypothyroidism and near-normal pituitary-thyroid feedback

item.vignette: A 9-year-old girl has chronic constipation, delayed linear growth, delayed bone age, and disproportionate short limbs. She has bradycardia but no goiter. Thyroid studies repeatedly show low-normal free thyroxine, high-normal triiodothyronine, a low T4-to-T3 ratio, and a normal thyroid-stimulating hormone concentration. Her mother has milder constipation and short stature.
item.lead_in: Which diagnosis best explains the clinical phenotype despite the absence of markedly elevated TSH?

options.A: Resistance to thyroid hormone beta due to THRB mutation
options.B: MCT8 deficiency due to SLC16A2 mutation
options.C: Resistance to thyroid hormone alpha due to a dominant-negative THRA variant

item.tested_construct: Dominant-negative THRA variants cause resistance to thyroid hormone alpha, producing hypothyroid features in TRα-predominant tissues such as bone and gastrointestinal tract with low-normal T4, high-normal T3, low T4/T3 ratio, and relatively preserved TSH feedback.

explanation.key_explanation: TRα1 is prominent in bone, gastrointestinal tract, heart, and other tissues. Dominant-negative THRA variants can therefore cause growth retardation, skeletal dysplasia/delayed bone age, constipation, and bradycardia while the pituitary-thyroid axis is much less perturbed than in THRB-mediated resistance; low-normal T4 and high-normal T3 are characteristic clues.

distractor_explanations.A: Option A proposes 'Resistance to thyroid hormone beta due to THRB mutation'. It is not selected because it does not account for constipation, skeletal growth delay, low-normal T4, high-normal T3, low T4/T3 ratio, and normal TSH in an autosomal-dominant pattern; THRB-mediated resistance typically causes clearly elevated circulating T4/T3 with nonsuppressed TSH and often goiter, rather than this low T4/T3-ratio tissue-hypothyroid phenotype.
distractor_explanations.B: Option B proposes 'MCT8 deficiency due to SLC16A2 mutation'. It is not selected because it does not account for constipation, skeletal growth delay, low-normal T4, high-normal T3, low T4/T3 ratio, and normal TSH in an autosomal-dominant pattern; MCT8 deficiency is an X-linked neurodevelopmental disorder in males with severe neurologic impairment and a different thyroid profile.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. TRα1 is prominent in bone, gastrointestinal tract, heart, and other tissues. Dominant-negative THRA variants can therefore cause growth retardation, skeletal dysplasia/delayed bone age, constipation, and bradycardia while the pituitary-thyroid axis is much less perturbed than in THRB-mediated resistance; low-normal T4 and high-normal T3 are characteristic clues.
distractor_explanations.D: Option D proposes 'Thyroid peroxidase deficiency'. It is not selected because it does not account for constipation, skeletal growth delay, low-normal T4, high-normal T3, low T4/T3 ratio, and normal TSH in an autosomal-dominant pattern; Thyroid peroxidase deficiency impairs hormone synthesis and generally causes primary hypothyroidism with elevated TSH and often goiter.
distractor_explanations.E: Option E proposes 'TSH receptor loss-of-function hypothyroidism'. It is not selected because it does not account for constipation, skeletal growth delay, low-normal T4, high-normal T3, low T4/T3 ratio, and normal TSH in an autosomal-dominant pattern; TSH-receptor loss causes primary thyroid hypofunction with elevated TSH rather than selective tissue resistance with preserved feedback.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize resistance to thyroid hormone alpha from tissue-specific hypothyroid features with a low T4/T3 ratio and relatively normal TSH.

evidence_map.claim: Option A proposes 'Resistance to thyroid hormone beta due to THRB mutation'. It is not selected because it does not account for constipation, skeletal growth delay, low-normal T4, high-normal T3, low T4/T3 ratio, and normal TSH in an autosomal-dominant pattern; THRB-mediated resistance typically causes clearly elevated circulating T4/T3 with nonsuppressed TSH and often goiter, rather than this low T4/T3-ratio tissue-hypothyroid phenotype.

item.vignette: A 3-week-old boy is admitted after recurrent fasting hypoglycemic seizures and prolonged cholestatic jaundice. Serum cortisol is very low and plasma ACTH is also low. Thyroid-stimulating hormone, free thyroxine, growth hormone, prolactin, and gonadotropins are appropriate for age. Pituitary MRI is normal. An older sibling died during a similar neonatal illness, and the parents are first cousins.
item.lead_in: Which genetic diagnosis best explains this selective pituitary hormone deficiency?

options.B: POU1F1-related combined GH, prolactin, and TSH deficiency

item.tested_construct: Biallelic TBX19 (TPIT) mutations impair terminal differentiation/function of pituitary POMC-expressing corticotrophs and are a major cause of neonatal-onset congenital isolated ACTH deficiency with preserved other pituitary axes.

explanation.key_explanation: TBX19 encodes TPIT, a T-box transcription factor restricted to pituitary POMC-expressing lineages and required for corticotroph differentiation and POMC/ACTH production. Recessive loss therefore causes low ACTH and cortisol with preservation of other pituitary hormones and a structurally normal pituitary.

distractor_explanations.A: Option A proposes 'PROP1-related combined pituitary hormone deficiency'. It is not selected because it does not account for isolated central hypocortisolism with low ACTH, preserved other pituitary hormones, normal pituitary imaging, neonatal hypoglycemia/cholestasis, and recessive inheritance; PROP1 defects cause combined and evolving pituitary hormone deficiencies rather than selective ACTH loss with all other axes preserved.
distractor_explanations.B: Option B proposes 'POU1F1-related combined GH, prolactin, and TSH deficiency'. It is not selected because it does not account for isolated central hypocortisolism with low ACTH, preserved other pituitary hormones, normal pituitary imaging, neonatal hypoglycemia/cholestasis, and recessive inheritance; POU1F1 defects primarily impair GH, prolactin, and TSH, the opposite of the preserved pattern in this infant.
distractor_explanations.C: Option C proposes 'NR0B1-related adrenal hypoplasia congenita'. It is not selected because it does not account for isolated central hypocortisolism with low ACTH, preserved other pituitary hormones, normal pituitary imaging, neonatal hypoglycemia/cholestasis, and recessive inheritance; NR0B1 causes primary adrenal hypoplasia with high ACTH, often accompanied later by hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; ACTH is low here.
distractor_explanations.D: Option D proposes 'MC2R-related familial glucocorticoid deficiency'. item.vignette: A male fetus develops severe polyhydramnios at 24 weeks of gestation and is delivered prematurely. During the first days of life, the infant has massive polyuria, hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis, hypokalemia, and markedly increased renin and aldosterone concentrations. Renal ultrasonography shows no obstruction. Over the next several weeks, the salt wasting and polyuria spontaneously resolve without a chronic electrolyte requirement. Two maternal male relatives had similar premature births.
item.lead_in: Which diagnosis best explains this severe but transient X-linked antenatal salt-wasting syndrome?
item.tested_construct: MAGED2 mutations cause X-linked transient antenatal Bartter syndrome with early severe polyhydramnios, prematurity, neonatal salt wasting/polyuria, and spontaneous resolution as renal tubular transporter expression/function matures after birth.

explanation.key_explanation: MAGE-D2 supports expression/function of the salt cotransporters NKCC2 and NCC under fetal conditions. Pathogenic MAGED2 variants can produce profound fetal renal salt wasting and polyhydramnios, yet the phenotype characteristically resolves spontaneously within weeks after premature birth, distinguishing it from persistent monogenic Bartter syndromes.

distractor_explanations.A: Option A proposes 'SLC12A1-associated classic antenatal Bartter syndrome'. It is not selected because it does not account for very early polyhydramnios, X-linked male clustering, neonatal Bartter physiology, and spontaneous complete resolution within weeks; SLC12A1 loss produces persistent NKCC2-dependent antenatal Bartter physiology rather than a characteristic self-limited X-linked syndrome.
distractor_explanations.B: Option B proposes 'KCNJ1-associated antenatal Bartter syndrome'. It is not selected because it does not account for very early polyhydramnios, X-linked male clustering, neonatal Bartter physiology, and spontaneous complete resolution within weeks; ROMK/KCNJ1 Bartter syndrome can present antenatally but is not expected to resolve completely within weeks and is not X-linked.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. MAGE-D2 supports expression/function of the salt cotransporters NKCC2 and NCC under fetal conditions. Pathogenic MAGED2 variants can produce profound fetal renal salt wasting and polyhydramnios, yet the phenotype characteristically resolves spontaneously within weeks after premature birth, distinguishing it from persistent monogenic Bartter syndromes.
distractor_explanations.D: Option D proposes 'CLCNKB-associated classic Bartter syndrome'. It is not selected because it does not account for very early polyhydramnios, X-linked male clustering, neonatal Bartter physiology, and spontaneous complete resolution within weeks; CLCNKB-associated disease is generally persistent and lacks the classic severe transient fetal phenotype linked to MAGED2.
distractor_explanations.E: Option E proposes 'SLC12A3-associated Gitelman syndrome'. It is not selected because it does not account for very early polyhydramnios, X-linked male clustering, neonatal Bartter physiology, and spontaneous complete resolution within weeks; Gitelman syndrome presents later with distal-convoluted-tubule salt wasting, hypomagnesemia, and hypocalciuria rather than severe fetal polyhydramnios and neonatal polyuria.

item.vignette: A 20-year-old man develops severe flank pain and acute kidney injury after an intense sprint workout. His serum uric acid concentration is 0.8 mg/dL between episodes, and fractional excretion of urate is markedly increased. Genetic testing shows biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC22A12. There is no nephrolithiasis or evidence of Fanconi syndrome.
item.lead_in: Which renal transport process is most directly impaired by this mutation?

options.A: Apical reabsorption of urate from the proximal tubular lumen by URAT1
options.B: Basolateral secretion of urate into proximal tubular cells by OAT1
options.C: Apical secretion of urate into the tubular lumen by ABCG2
options.E: Apical cystine and dibasic amino-acid reabsorption by the b0,+ transporter

item.tested_construct: SLC22A12 encodes apical proximal-tubule URAT1, a major urate reabsorptive transporter; loss causes renal hypouricemia with increased urate excretion and can predispose to exercise-induced acute kidney injury.

explanation.key_explanation: URAT1 is located on the apical membrane of proximal tubular cells and mediates reabsorption of filtered urate from the tubular lumen. Biallelic SLC22A12 loss reduces urate reabsorption, causing hypouricemia and high fractional urate excretion; renal hypouricemia is associated with exercise-induced acute kidney injury.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. URAT1 is located on the apical membrane of proximal tubular cells and mediates reabsorption of filtered urate from the tubular lumen. Biallelic SLC22A12 loss reduces urate reabsorption, causing hypouricemia and high fractional urate excretion; renal hypouricemia is associated with exercise-induced acute kidney injury.
distractor_explanations.B: Option B proposes 'Basolateral secretion of urate into proximal tubular cells by OAT1'. It is not selected because it does not account for marked renal urate wasting with biallelic SLC22A12 loss and exercise-associated acute kidney injury; OAT1 is a basolateral organic-anion transporter involved in proximal-tubule secretion, not the apical URAT1 reabsorptive step encoded by SLC22A12.
distractor_explanations.C: Option C proposes 'Apical secretion of urate into the tubular lumen by ABCG2'. It is not selected because it does not account for marked renal urate wasting with biallelic SLC22A12 loss and exercise-associated acute kidney injury; ABCG2 participates in urate secretion; increased or preserved secretion does not identify the specific SLC22A12 loss in the stem.
distractor_explanations.D: Option D proposes 'Basolateral sodium-bicarbonate cotransport by NBCe1'. It is not selected because it does not account for marked renal urate wasting with biallelic SLC22A12 loss and exercise-associated acute kidney injury; NBCe1 is encoded by SLC4A4 and mediates bicarbonate exit, producing proximal RTA when defective rather than isolated renal hypouricemia.
distractor_explanations.E: Option E proposes 'Apical cystine and dibasic amino-acid reabsorption by the b0,+ transporter'. It is not selected because it does not account for marked renal urate wasting with biallelic SLC22A12 loss and exercise-associated acute kidney injury; The b0,+ amino-acid transporter is involved in cystinuria and does not mediate urate reabsorption.

explanation.educational_objective: Identify URAT1/SLC22A12 as an apical proximal-tubule urate reabsorptive transporter and connect loss of function to renal hypouricemia.

evidence_map.claim: Correct. URAT1 is located on the apical membrane of proximal tubular cells and mediates reabsorption of filtered urate from the tubular lumen. Biallelic SLC22A12 loss reduces urate reabsorption, causing hypouricemia and high fractional urate excretion; renal hypouricemia is associated with exercise-induced acute kidney injury.

item.vignette: A 29-year-old woman has progressive proteinuria and declining kidney function. Kidney biopsy shows focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. Since adolescence she has also had distal leg weakness, pes cavus, reduced ankle reflexes, and slowed motor nerve conduction. Her father required kidney transplantation in his 40s and used ankle-foot orthoses for a similar neuropathy. Testing for PMP22 duplication and MPZ variants is negative.
item.lead_in: Which genetic disorder most specifically unifies the glomerular and peripheral nerve phenotypes?

options.E: INF2-associated Charcot-Marie-Tooth neuropathy with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis

item.tested_construct: Heterozygous INF2 mutations can cause autosomal-dominant FSGS together with an intermediate Charcot-Marie-Tooth neuropathy by perturbing actin/cytoskeletal pathways important in podocytes and Schwann cells.

explanation.key_explanation: INF2 encodes a formin that regulates actin dynamics and is expressed in podocytes and Schwann cells. Specific dominant INF2 variants are strongly associated with the combination of FSGS and Charcot-Marie-Tooth neuropathy, providing a single molecular explanation for renal and peripheral nerve disease across generations.

distractor_explanations.A: Option A proposes 'NPHS2-associated steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome'. It is not selected because it does not account for autosomal-dominant FSGS together with a PMP22/MPZ-negative inherited peripheral neuropathy characterized by pes cavus and distal weakness; NPHS2 causes recessive podocyte disease but does not explain an autosomal-dominant inherited peripheral neuropathy.
distractor_explanations.B: Option B proposes 'COL4A5-associated Alport syndrome'. It is not selected because it does not account for autosomal-dominant FSGS together with a PMP22/MPZ-negative inherited peripheral neuropathy characterized by pes cavus and distal weakness; Alport syndrome links glomerular basement-membrane disease with hearing and ocular abnormalities rather than Charcot-Marie-Tooth neuropathy and FSGS.
distractor_explanations.C: Option C proposes 'PMP22-associated Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1A'. It is not selected because it does not account for autosomal-dominant FSGS together with a PMP22/MPZ-negative inherited peripheral neuropathy characterized by pes cavus and distal weakness; PMP22 duplication can explain the neuropathy but not the familial FSGS, and PMP22 testing is negative.
distractor_explanations.D: Option D proposes 'LMX1B-associated nail-patella syndrome'. It is not selected because it does not account for autosomal-dominant FSGS together with a PMP22/MPZ-negative inherited peripheral neuropathy characterized by pes cavus and distal weakness; LMX1B can cause glomerular disease but is associated with nail, patellar, and skeletal abnormalities rather than this inherited demyelinating/intermediate neuropathy.

Specific dominant INF2 variants are strongly associated with the combination of FSGS and Charcot-Marie-Tooth neuropathy, providing a single molecular explanation for renal and peripheral nerve disease across generations.

item.vignette: A 17-year-old boy develops nephrotic-range proteinuria. Kidney biopsy shows focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. His mother and maternal grandfather developed similar disease as young adults. Sequencing identifies a heterozygous missense variant in TRPC6. Patch-clamp studies of cells expressing the mutant channel show increased agonist-evoked inward current and delayed channel inactivation.
item.lead_in: Which cellular change most directly links this mutation to podocyte injury?

options.A: Reduced slit-diaphragm nephrin expression from a recessive NPHS1 defect
options.B: Reduced mitochondrial coenzyme Q10 synthesis in podocytes
options.C: Loss of glomerular basement-membrane laminin beta2
options.D: Excess calcium entry through a gain-of-function TRPC6 cation channel
options.E: Failure of podocyte actin polymerization due to complete INF2 loss

item.tested_construct: Gain-of-function TRPC6 variants increase cation current and calcium entry in podocytes, perturbing calcium-dependent signaling and cytoskeletal homeostasis and causing autosomal-dominant FSGS.

explanation.key_explanation: TRPC6 is a calcium-permeable nonselective cation channel expressed in podocytes. Disease-causing dominant variants can increase channel activity or impair inactivation, producing excessive calcium influx and downstream signaling that disrupts podocyte structure and promotes FSGS.

distractor_explanations.A: Option A proposes 'Reduced slit-diaphragm nephrin expression from a recessive NPHS1 defect'. It is not selected because it does not account for autosomal-dominant FSGS with a TRPC6 variant that directly increases inward current and delays channel inactivation; NPHS1 disease is usually recessive and affects nephrin at the slit diaphragm; it does not explain the demonstrated hyperactive TRPC6 current.
distractor_explanations.B: Option B proposes 'Reduced mitochondrial coenzyme Q10 synthesis in podocytes'. It is not selected because it does not account for autosomal-dominant FSGS with a TRPC6 variant that directly increases inward current and delays channel inactivation; CoQ10-biosynthesis disorders can cause steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome but do not produce the specific gain-of-function cation-channel phenotype.
distractor_explanations.C: Option C proposes 'Loss of glomerular basement-membrane laminin beta2'. It is not selected because it does not account for autosomal-dominant FSGS with a TRPC6 variant that directly increases inward current and delays channel inactivation; LAMB2 loss causes Pierson syndrome and a basement-membrane structural defect, not increased agonist-evoked calcium current.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. TRPC6 is a calcium-permeable nonselective cation channel expressed in podocytes. Disease-causing dominant variants can increase channel activity or impair inactivation, producing excessive calcium influx and downstream signaling that disrupts podocyte structure and promotes FSGS.
distractor_explanations.E: Option E proposes 'Failure of podocyte actin polymerization due to complete INF2 loss'. It is not selected because it does not account for autosomal-dominant FSGS with a TRPC6 variant that directly increases inward current and delays channel inactivation; INF2 disease involves a formin/actin-regulatory pathway; the functional study here directly localizes the defect to increased TRPC6 channel activity.

item.vignette: A newborn girl develops massive proteinuria and hypoalbuminemia during the first week of life. Examination shows fixed small pupils that do not dilate normally. Kidney biopsy shows diffuse mesangial sclerosis. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in LAMB2. Electron microscopy shows a structurally abnormal glomerular basement membrane.
item.lead_in: Loss of which normal extracellular-matrix component most directly accounts for the renal phenotype?

options.A: Type IV collagen alpha5 chain in the glomerular basement membrane
options.B: Laminin beta2 within the laminin network of the glomerular basement membrane
options.C: Nephrin spanning the podocyte slit diaphragm
options.D: Alpha3 integrin on the basal surface of podocytes
options.E: Podocin within the slit-diaphragm signaling complex

item.tested_construct: LAMB2 encodes laminin beta2, a critical component of glomerular basement-membrane laminin; biallelic loss causes Pierson syndrome with congenital nephrotic syndrome/diffuse mesangial sclerosis and characteristic microcoria.

explanation.key_explanation: Laminin beta2 is incorporated into laminin heterotrimers of the mature glomerular basement membrane and is also important in ocular structures. Biallelic LAMB2 deficiency disrupts the filtration barrier, causing congenital nephrosis and diffuse mesangial sclerosis, while microcoria provides a highly specific syndromic clue.

distractor_explanations.A: Option A proposes 'Type IV collagen alpha5 chain in the glomerular basement membrane'. It is not selected because it does not account for congenital nephrotic syndrome with diffuse mesangial sclerosis, microcoria, and biallelic LAMB2 variants; COL4A5 defects cause X-linked Alport syndrome with hearing/ocular abnormalities but not the classic microcoria-congenital-nephrosis Pierson phenotype.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. Laminin beta2 is incorporated into laminin heterotrimers of the mature glomerular basement membrane and is also important in ocular structures. Biallelic LAMB2 deficiency disrupts the filtration barrier, causing congenital nephrosis and diffuse mesangial sclerosis, while microcoria provides a highly specific syndromic clue.
distractor_explanations.C: Option C proposes 'Nephrin spanning the podocyte slit diaphragm'. It is not selected because it does not account for congenital nephrotic syndrome with diffuse mesangial sclerosis, microcoria, and biallelic LAMB2 variants; Nephrin is a slit-diaphragm protein encoded by NPHS1 rather than the extracellular basement-membrane component encoded by LAMB2.
distractor_explanations.D: Option D proposes 'Alpha3 integrin on the basal surface of podocytes'. It is not selected because it does not account for congenital nephrotic syndrome with diffuse mesangial sclerosis, microcoria, and biallelic LAMB2 variants; Integrin alpha3 is a podocyte cell-surface adhesion receptor and is not the laminin beta2 extracellular-matrix protein lost in this genotype.
distractor_explanations.E: Option E proposes 'Podocin within the slit-diaphragm signaling complex'. It is not selected because it does not account for congenital nephrotic syndrome with diffuse mesangial sclerosis, microcoria, and biallelic LAMB2 variants; Podocin is an intracellular membrane-associated slit-diaphragm protein encoded by NPHS2 and does not explain the LAMB2-specific ocular and basement-membrane phenotype.

explanation.educational_objective: Identify laminin beta2 as the glomerular basement-membrane component defective in LAMB2-associated Pierson syndrome.
